newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala volcano erupts, villagers evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala volcano erupts, villagers evacuated.

text.p: A volcano near Guatemala City erupted on Monday, setting off mile-long lava flows and spewing a column of ash nearly 2 miles (a kilometre) into the air, officials said.

For the second time in a month, villagers were evacuated from the slopes of the Pacaya volcano after a series of eruptions beginning late in the morning and getting stronger at about 3 p.m. EDT (2000 GMT). There were no reports of injuries.
"We thought this was going to be moderate but it's strong," volcanologist Gustavo Chigna, of the National Institute of Seismology, said in a telephone interview.
Chigna said Monday's explosion was stronger than another one at the same volcano exactly one month ago. The volcano is located some 24 miles (40 km) south of the capital.

Officials began evacuating several dozen people from the village of El Caracol and placed other towns nearby on alert, said Colonel Oscar Guillermo Hernandez, head of Guatemala's National Emergency Committee.
The 8,421-foot (2,552-meter) Pacaya is one of several active volcanos across Guatemala, and it erupts regularly.

Just after midnight on Oct 11, the volcano erupted in its biggest explosion since 1987. A two-hour string of fiery explosions and molten lava flows were visible against the night sky from downtown Guatemala City. About 100 villagers were evacuated that night and no one was injured or killed.
